purpose: Test whether a regime signal built only from series with genuine long history can reduce drawdown on a long-only book without destroying return, over a span that contains 2000, 2008, 2020 and 2022.

coverage_finding_that_shaped_this.problem: The project's existing regime feature set is anchored on the VIX term-structure slope, and VIX3M begins 2009-09-18. Anything built on the slope cannot be tested through the dot-com crash or the global financial crisis, which are the two regimes Step 191's gate most needs.
coverage_finding_that_shaped_this.consequence: The overlay is built from VIX level and NFCI only. This is a weaker signal than the slope-based one already in the repository, and it is the only one that can be honestly tested across four bear markets.

gates.name: vix_percentile
gates.rule: cut exposure when the VIX close sits above its own trailing 5-year percentile threshold

gates.name: nfci_positive
gates.rule: cut exposure when the Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index is above zero, meaning conditions are tighter than average

publication_lags.VIX: 1 trading day, because the close is known only after the close
publication_lags.NFCI: 8 calendar days, which is longer than the actual weekly release lag and is chosen to be conservative rather than exact

hypotheses: A regime gate that only fires after a shock is priced in will cut drawdown and cut return by more, which is the usual failure mode and must be visible.
If any gate improves drawdown while keeping return within a few points, it is worth carrying as an overlay.
If the gates work on SPY but not on the trend sleeve, that is evidence the sleeve already contains its own de-risking.
not_claimed: Testing on SPY and ETF books is a proxy. The SEC equity books start 2022-12 and cannot be tested across these regimes at all; that gap is exactly what Step 191 recorded and this does not close it.
No threshold is selected. Both VIX percentile thresholds and both gated exposures are reported in full.
